name: Stripe
setup_hint: Create a Stripe Secret Key at Dashboard > Developers > API keys (starts with sk_live_ or sk_test_).

name: PayPal
description: PayPal REST API for payments and orders
setup_hint: Create a PayPal app at developer.paypal.com to get client_id and secret; exchange via Basic Auth at /v1/oauth2/token for a Bearer token.

name: Square
setup_hint: Get an access token from Square Developer Portal; include Square-Version header (e.g., 2025-01-22) on every request.

auth_options.label: Personal Access Token (PAT)
auth_options.description: Create a PAT in the Square Developer Portal under your application.

auth_options.label: OAuth 2.0 (Authorization Code)
auth_options.description: Register an OAuth app in the Square Developer Portal, configure redirect URIs.

name: Shopify
setup_hint: Create a custom app in Shopify Admin > Settings > Apps and development; copy the Admin API access token (header: X-Shopify-Access-Token).

name: Salesforce
setup_hint: Create a Connected App in Salesforce Setup > App Manager; note client_id and client_secret for OAuth2 authorization code flow.

name: HubSpot
setup_hint: Create a private app in HubSpot > Settings > Integrations > Private Apps; copy the access token, or use OAuth for public apps.

name: Pipedrive
setup_hint: Find API token under Settings > Personal Preferences > API, or register an OAuth app in the Developer Hub.

auth_options.label: API Token (Query Param)
auth_options.description: Find token under Settings > Personal Preferences > API. Passed as ?api_token= query parameter (v1 only).

auth_options.label: OAuth Token (Bearer)
auth_options.description: Use OAuth bearer token from the Pipedrive Developer Hub OAuth flow.

auth_options.label: OAuth 2.0
auth_options.description: Register an OAuth app in the Pipedrive Developer Hub for Authorization Code flow.

name: Zoho CRM
setup_hint: Register a self-client at Zoho API Console, generate a grant token with CRM scopes, exchange for tokens. Access tokens expire in 1 hour.

name: Jira
setup_hint: Choose: (1) API Token — create at id.atlassian.com/manage-profile/security/api-tokens, use Basic Auth. (2) OAuth 2.0 — register app at developer.atlassian.com.

auth_options.label: API Token (Basic Auth)
auth_options.description: Create an API token at id.atlassian.com/manage-profile/security/api-tokens. Use email as username, token as password. Base URL: https://{domain}.atlassian.net/rest/api/3

auth_options.label: OAuth 2.0 (3LO)
auth_options.description: Register an OAuth 2.0 app at developer.atlassian.com/console/myapps/. Requires audience=api.atlassian.com parameter. Base URL: https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/{cloudId}/rest/api/3

name: Linear
setup_hint: Create a personal API key at linear.app/settings/api or register an OAuth app under Settings > API > OAuth Applications.

name: Asana
setup_hint: Create a Personal Access Token at app.asana.com/0/my-apps, or register an OAuth app there.

auth_options.label: Personal Access Token (PAT)
auth_options.description: Create a PAT at app.asana.com/0/my-apps. Use as Bearer token.

auth_options.label: OAuth 2.0 (Authorization Code)
auth_options.description: Register an OAuth app at app.asana.com/0/my-apps for Authorization Code flow.

name: Monday.com
setup_hint: Find your personal API token under avatar > Developers > My Access Tokens, or create an OAuth app in the Developer Center.

name: Trello
setup_hint: Create a Power-Up at trello.com/power-ups/admin to get an API key, then authorize a token via /1/authorize URL.

name: ClickUp
setup_hint: Find your personal API token under Settings > Apps in ClickUp (starts with pk_), or create an OAuth app.

auth_options.label: Personal Token
auth_options.description: Find your personal API token under Settings > Apps in ClickUp (starts with pk_).

auth_options.label: OAuth 2.0 (Authorization Code)
auth_options.description: Create an OAuth app in the ClickUp Developer Portal.

name: Slack
setup_hint: Create a Slack app at api.slack.com/apps, add Bot Token Scopes, install to workspace, copy the Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb-).

name: Discord
setup_hint: Create an app at discord.com/developers/applications, add a Bot, copy the token, use as `Authorization: Bot {token}`.

auth_options.label: Bot Token
auth_options.description: Create a Bot in the Discord Developer Portal, copy the token. Uses 'Bot' prefix in Authorization header.

auth_options.label: OAuth 2.0 (User OAuth)
auth_options.description: Register an OAuth2 app at discord.com/developers/applications for user-level access.

name: Twilio
description: Twilio SMS, Voice, and Messaging API
setup_hint: Sign up at twilio.com, grab Account SID + Auth Token from Console, use as Basic Auth (SID=username, token=password).

name: SendGrid
setup_hint: Generate an API key under Settings > API Keys (starts with SG.), pass as Bearer token.

name: Mailchimp
setup_hint: Generate an API key from Account & Billing > Extras > API Keys; the suffix (e.g., -us19) determines your data center for the base URL.

auth_options.label: API Key (Basic Auth)
auth_options.description: Use any string as username and the API key as password for Basic Auth.

auth_options.label: OAuth Token (Bearer)
auth_options.description: Use an OAuth-obtained access token as Bearer.

auth_options.label: OAuth 2.0
auth_options.description: Register an OAuth app in the Mailchimp Developer Portal.

name: Notion
setup_hint: Create an internal integration at notion.so/my-integrations, copy the token (ntn_), share pages with the integration.

name: Airtable
setup_hint: Create a personal access token at airtable.com/create/tokens with scopes for the bases you need.

name: Confluence
setup_hint: Create an API token at id.atlassian.com for Basic Auth, or register an OAuth 2.0 (3LO) app at developer.atlassian.com.

auth_options.label: API Token (Basic Auth)
auth_options.description: Create an API token at id.atlassian.com/manage-profile/security/api-tokens. Use email as username, token as password.

auth_options.label: OAuth 2.0 (3LO)
auth_options.description: Register an OAuth 2.0 app at developer.atlassian.com/console/myapps/. Same Atlassian OAuth app works for Jira and Confluence.

name: Dropbox
setup_hint: Create an app at dropbox.com/developers/apps, choose 'Scoped access', configure scopes in Permissions tab, note App key and secret.

auth_options.label: OAuth 2.0 (PKCE supported)
auth_options.description: Only auth method. Create app at dropbox.com/developers/apps, use Authorization Code flow with or without PKCE.

name: Box
setup_hint: Create a Box app at app.box.com/developers/console, choose OAuth 2.0, configure redirect URI, note Client ID and Secret.

name: Google Workspace
setup_hint: Create a Google Cloud project, enable APIs, configure OAuth consent screen, create OAuth 2.0 credentials.

auth_options.label: OAuth 2.0 (Auth Code)
auth_options.description: Standard OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow for user-level access.

auth_options.label: Service Account (JWT)
auth_options.description: Use a service account JSON key for server-to-server access without user interaction.

name: Google Gmail
setup_hint: Create a Google Cloud project, enable Gmail API, configure OAuth consent screen, create OAuth 2.0 credentials.

auth_options.label: OAuth 2.0 (Auth Code)
auth_options.description: Standard OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow for user-level access.

auth_options.label: Service Account (JWT)
auth_options.description: Use a service account with domain-wide delegation for server-to-server access.

name: Google Calendar
setup_hint: Create a Google Cloud project, enable Calendar API, configure OAuth consent screen, create OAuth 2.0 credentials.

auth_options.label: OAuth 2.0 (Auth Code)
auth_options.description: Standard OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow for user-level access.

auth_options.label: Service Account (JWT)
auth_options.description: Use a service account for server-to-server access without user interaction.

name: Google Drive
setup_hint: Create a Google Cloud project, enable Drive API, configure OAuth consent screen, create OAuth 2.0 credentials.

auth_options.label: OAuth 2.0 (Auth Code)
auth_options.description: Standard OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow for user-level access.

auth_options.label: Service Account (JWT)
auth_options.description: Use a service account for server-to-server access without user interaction.

name: Google Docs
setup_hint: Create a Google Cloud project, enable Docs API, configure OAuth consent screen, create OAuth 2.0 credentials.

auth_options.label: OAuth 2.0 (Auth Code)
auth_options.description: Standard OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow for user-level access.

auth_options.label: Service Account (JWT)
auth_options.description: Use a service account for server-to-server access without user interaction.

name: Google Sheets
setup_hint: Create a Google Cloud project, enable Sheets API, configure OAuth consent screen, create OAuth 2.0 credentials.

auth_options.label: OAuth 2.0 (Auth Code)
auth_options.description: Standard OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow for user-level access.

auth_options.label: Service Account (JWT)
auth_options.description: Use a service account for server-to-server access without user interaction.

name: Google Chat
setup_hint: Create a Google Cloud project, enable Chat API, configure Chat app, set up OAuth, publish to Workspace domain.

auth_options.label: OAuth 2.0 (Auth Code)
auth_options.description: Standard OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow for user-level access.

auth_options.label: Service Account (JWT)
auth_options.description: Use a service account for server-to-server access. Requires Google Workspace domain.

name: Google Cloud Storage
setup_hint: Create a Google Cloud project, enable Cloud Storage JSON API, create a service account with Storage Object Admin IAM role.

auth_options.label: OAuth 2.0 (Auth Code)
auth_options.description: Standard OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow for user-level access.

auth_options.label: Service Account (JWT)
auth_options.description: Use a service account JSON key for server-to-server access.

name: Microsoft Graph
setup_hint: Register an app in Azure Portal > App registrations, add Microsoft Graph API permissions, generate a client secret, use tenant-specific or /common/ OAuth endpoints.

auth_options.label: OAuth 2.0 (Auth Code)
auth_options.description: Authorization Code flow for delegated user access. Use /common/ for multi-tenant or tenant GUID for single-tenant.

auth_options.label: OAuth 2.0 (Client Credentials)
auth_options.description: Client Credentials flow for app-only access without a user. Requires admin consent for application permissions.

name: Microsoft Outlook
description: Microsoft Outlook mail API via Graph
setup_hint: Register an app in Azure Portal, add Mail.Read/Mail.Send permissions; for app-level access to all mailboxes, use application permissions with admin consent.

auth_options.label: OAuth 2.0 (Auth Code)
auth_options.description: Authorization Code flow for delegated user access to their own mailbox.

auth_options.label: OAuth 2.0 (Client Credentials)
auth_options.description: Client Credentials for app-only access to all mailboxes. Requires admin consent.

name: Microsoft Teams
setup_hint: Register an app in Azure Portal with Teams-specific Graph permissions; many Teams permissions require admin consent.

auth_options.label: OAuth 2.0 (Auth Code)
auth_options.description: Authorization Code flow for delegated user access.

auth_options.label: OAuth 2.0 (Client Credentials)
auth_options.description: Client Credentials for app-only access. Most Teams permissions require admin consent.

name: Microsoft SharePoint
setup_hint: Register an app in Azure Portal with Sites.Read.All or Sites.ReadWrite.All Graph permissions; use Graph API (not legacy SharePoint REST _api).

auth_options.label: OAuth 2.0 (Auth Code)
auth_options.description: Authorization Code flow for delegated user access.

auth_options.label: OAuth 2.0 (Client Credentials)
auth_options.description: Client Credentials for app-only access. Sites.ReadWrite.All grants access to ALL sites.

name: Microsoft OneDrive
description: Microsoft OneDrive file storage API via Graph
setup_hint: Register an app in Azure Portal with Files.Read/ReadWrite permissions; use /me/drive for personal, Sites.Read.All for org SharePoint drives.

auth_options.label: OAuth 2.0 (Auth Code)
auth_options.description: Authorization Code flow for delegated user access to personal OneDrive.

auth_options.label: OAuth 2.0 (Client Credentials)
auth_options.description: Client Credentials for app-only access. Files.Read is personal only — org drives need Sites.Read.All.

name: GitHub
setup_hint: Create a PAT at github.com/settings/tokens, or register an OAuth App under Developer Settings.

name: GitLab
setup_hint: Choose: (1) PAT — create at User Settings > Access Tokens, use PRIVATE-TOKEN header. (2) OAuth 2.0 — register app under Applications.

auth_options.label: Personal Access Token (PAT)
auth_options.description: Create at User Settings > Access Tokens with needed scopes. Pass as PRIVATE-TOKEN header.

auth_options.label: OAuth 2.0
auth_options.description: Register an OAuth app under User Settings > Applications. Uses standard Authorization: Bearer flow.

name: Bitbucket
setup_hint: Create an API token at id.atlassian.com for Basic Auth, or register an OAuth consumer under Workspace Settings.

auth_options.label: App Password (Basic Auth)
auth_options.description: Create an app password at Bitbucket Settings > App passwords. Use email + app password as Basic Auth.

auth_options.label: OAuth 2.0
auth_options.description: Register an OAuth consumer under Workspace Settings. Token endpoint is /access_token (not /token).

name: CircleCI
setup_hint: Generate a Personal API Token from User Settings in CircleCI, pass as `Circle-Token` header.

name: Vercel
setup_hint: Create an access token at vercel.com/account/tokens. For team resources, append `?teamId={id}`.

name: Cloudflare
description: Cloudflare API for DNS, CDN, Workers, and security
setup_hint: Go to My Profile > API Tokens in Cloudflare dashboard, create a scoped API Token, use as Bearer.

name: AWS S3
setup_hint: Create an IAM user, generate Access Key ID + Secret Access Key, note target S3 region and bucket.

name: AWS Lambda
setup_hint: Create IAM user/role with Lambda permissions, generate Access Key ID + Secret, note function region.

name: AWS DynamoDB
setup_hint: Create IAM user/role with DynamoDB permissions, generate keys, note region.

name: AWS SES
setup_hint: Create IAM user with SES permissions, verify sender email/domain, request production access to leave sandbox.

name: AWS SQS
setup_hint: Create IAM user/role with SQS permissions, note queue URL and region.

name: Azure DevOps
setup_hint: Choose: (1) PAT — create at User Settings > Personal Access Tokens, use Basic Auth. (2) OAuth — register Entra ID app for service principal access.

auth_options.label: Personal Access Token (PAT)
auth_options.description: Go to User Settings > Personal Access Tokens, create PAT with required scopes. Use Basic Auth: base64 of ':' + PAT (empty username).

auth_options.label: OAuth 2.0 (Microsoft Entra ID)
auth_options.description: Register an app in Azure Portal, use Entra ID OAuth2 endpoints with scope 499b84ac-1321-427f-aa17-267ca6975798/.default

name: Azure Blob Storage
setup_hint: Create Storage Account in Azure Portal, find access keys under 'Access keys', or generate SAS token.

name: Azure Functions
setup_hint: Register app in Microsoft Entra ID, grant Contributor role on Function App, obtain client ID, secret, tenant ID.

name: DigitalOcean
setup_hint: In DigitalOcean Control Panel, go to API > Tokens, generate PAT (dop_v1_) with read/write scope.

name: PostgreSQL
setup_hint: Provide a PostgreSQL DSN: postgres://user:password@host:5432/database. Engine introspects tables via information_schema.

name: Microsoft SQL Server
setup_hint: Provide an MSSQL connection string: mssql://user:password@hostname:1433/database?encrypt=true. For Azure SQL, enable 'Allow Azure services' in firewall rules.

auth_options.label: SQL Authentication (DSN)
auth_options.description: Provide username and password in the connection string.

auth_options.label: Microsoft Entra ID (Azure SQL)
auth_options.description: Use Entra ID token-based auth for Azure SQL. Register app in Azure Portal, assign SQL roles.

name: MySQL
setup_hint: Provide a MySQL DSN: mysql://user:password@hostname:3306/database?ssl=true. Works with MySQL 5.7+, MySQL 8.x, and MariaDB 10.x+.

name: CockroachDB
setup_hint: Provide a CockroachDB DSN: postgresql://user:password@host:26257/defaultdb?sslmode=verify-full. Uses PostgreSQL wire protocol — fully compatible with the PostgreSQL driver.

name: Oracle ORDS
setup_hint: Oracle REST Data Services (ORDS) exposes a SQL execution API. For Oracle Cloud Autonomous DB, ORDS is always-on. For on-premise, deploy ORDS. POST SQL to /_/sql endpoint.

auth_options.label: Database Credentials
auth_options.description: Use your Oracle database username and password as Basic Auth credentials against the ORDS endpoint.

auth_options.label: OAuth 2.0 (ORDS Client)
auth_options.description: Register an OAuth client in ORDS: BEGIN OAUTH.create_client(...); Authorize via ORDS OAuth endpoints.

name: Supabase
setup_hint: Get project URL and API keys from Dashboard > Settings > API. Use `apikey` header with anon or service_role key.

name: Firebase
setup_hint: Enable Firestore in Firebase Console, create service account with Firestore Admin role.

name: Snowflake
setup_hint: Generate RSA key pair, assign public key via ALTER USER SET RSA_PUBLIC_KEY, sign JWTs with private key; or create OAuth security integration.

name: Datadog
setup_hint: In Datadog Org Settings, create API key and Application key; pass as `DD-API-KEY` and `DD-APPLICATION-KEY` headers.

name: PagerDuty
setup_hint: In PagerDuty, go to Integrations > API Access Keys, create REST API key, use as `Authorization: Token token={key}`.

auth_options.label: API Key (Token header)
auth_options.description: Create REST API key at Integrations > API Access Keys. Use as 'Authorization: Token token={key}'.

auth_options.label: OAuth 2.0
auth_options.description: Register an OAuth app in PagerDuty Developer Mode for Authorization Code flow.

name: Sentry
description: Sentry error tracking and performance API
setup_hint: Create auth token at sentry.io Settings > Auth Tokens with needed scopes, pass as Bearer.

name: ServiceNow
setup_hint: In ServiceNow, go to System OAuth > Application Registry to create an OAuth endpoint; use client_id/secret with instance token endpoint. Or use Basic Auth with admin credentials.

auth_options.label: Basic Auth
auth_options.description: Use ServiceNow admin username and password as Basic Auth credentials.

auth_options.label: OAuth 2.0
auth_options.description: Create an OAuth endpoint in System OAuth > Application Registry, use client_id/secret with instance token endpoint.

name: Okta
description: Okta identity and access management API
setup_hint: In Okta Admin Console, go to Security > API > Tokens for SSWS API key (header: `Authorization: SSWS {token}`), or register OAuth app under Applications.

auth_options.label: SSWS Token
auth_options.description: Create API token at Security > API > Tokens. Use as 'Authorization: SSWS {token}'.

auth_options.label: OAuth 2.0
auth_options.description: Register an OAuth app under Applications for Authorization Code or Client Credentials flow.

name: Auth0
setup_hint: Create a Machine-to-Machine app in Auth0 Dashboard, authorize for Management API with scopes, use client_credentials grant.

name: Intercom
setup_hint: In Intercom Developer Hub, create app, find access token under Authentication; for OAuth, configure redirect URIs.

name: Freshdesk
setup_hint: In Freshdesk, click Profile > Profile Settings, find API key on right sidebar, use as Basic Auth username with 'X' as password.

name: BambooHR
setup_hint: In BambooHR, gear icon > API Keys > Add New Key; use as Basic Auth username with 'x' as password. Or use OIDC OAuth flow.

auth_options.label: API Key (Basic Auth)
auth_options.description: Create API key in BambooHR settings, use as Basic Auth username with 'x' as password.

auth_options.label: OAuth 2.0 (OIDC)
auth_options.description: Use OIDC OAuth flow via id.bamboohr.com for token-based access.

name: Zendesk
setup_hint: Choose: (1) API Token — enable in Admin > APIs, use Basic Auth with email/token as username. (2) OAuth 2.0 — register client in Admin Center.

auth_options.label: API Token (Basic Auth)
auth_options.description: Enable Token Access in Admin > APIs, generate token. Basic Auth: username = email/token, password = API token.

auth_options.label: OAuth 2.0
auth_options.description: Register an OAuth client in Admin Center > Apps > OAuth Clients. Uses subdomain-specific endpoints.

name: Apple iCloud Calendar
setup_hint: Apple iCloud CalDAV requires an app-specific password: go to appleid.apple.com > Sign-In and Security > App-Specific Passwords. Use Apple ID email + app-specific password as Basic Auth.

name: Apple iCloud Contacts
setup_hint: Apple iCloud CardDAV requires an app-specific password: go to appleid.apple.com > Sign-In and Security > App-Specific Passwords.

name: CalDAV (Generic)
setup_hint: Provide your CalDAV server URL and credentials. Common servers: Nextcloud (/remote.php/dav), Google (apidata.googleusercontent.com/caldav/v2), Fastmail (caldav.fastmail.com).

auth_options.label: Username + Password
auth_options.description: Use your CalDAV server credentials as Basic Auth.

auth_options.label: OAuth 2.0 (Google, etc.)
auth_options.description: Some CalDAV servers (Google) support OAuth2. Configure with your provider's OAuth endpoints.

name: WebDAV (Generic)
setup_hint: Provide your WebDAV server URL and credentials. Common servers: Nextcloud, ownCloud, Apache mod_dav, Nginx DAV, Box (dav.box.com).

auth_options.label: Username + Password
auth_options.description: Use your WebDAV server credentials as Basic Auth.

auth_options.label: Bearer Token
auth_options.description: Some WebDAV servers support Bearer token auth.

name: SOAP (Generic)
setup_hint: Provide the SOAP endpoint URL. Append ?wsdl to fetch the service definition. Choose auth method: HTTP Basic, WS-Security (UsernameToken), or OAuth Bearer.

auth_options.label: HTTP Basic Auth
auth_options.description: Standard HTTP Basic Auth for the SOAP endpoint.

auth_options.label: WS-Security (UsernameToken)
auth_options.description: Username and password in the SOAP header via WS-Security. Configured in connector config.

auth_options.label: OAuth 2.0 Bearer
auth_options.description: Bearer token in HTTP Authorization header for modern SOAP services.

name: SAP SOAP
setup_hint: SAP exposes SOAP services via /sap/bc/srt/. Find your WSDL at the service endpoint + ?wsdl. Use SAP technical user credentials for Basic Auth.

name: ServiceNow SOAP
description: ServiceNow SOAP API for legacy integrations
setup_hint: ServiceNow exposes SOAP via /{tableName}.do?WSDL. Use admin credentials for Basic Auth.

name: gRPC Connect
setup_hint: Connect RPC services expose gRPC over standard HTTP/1.1. Provide the base URL and an auth token if required. Uses JSON encoding by default (protobuf optional).

name: gRPC Native
description: Native gRPC over HTTP/2 with protobuf
setup_hint: Provide the gRPC server address (host:port). If the server has reflection enabled, operations are auto-discovered. Otherwise, provide .proto files.

name: MQTT
setup_hint: Provide MQTT broker URL (mqtt:// or mqtts:// for TLS). Username/password if required. Common brokers: Mosquitto, HiveMQ, EMQX, AWS IoT Core, Azure IoT Hub.

auth_options.label: Username + Password
auth_options.description: MQTT CONNECT packet carries username/password. Standard for most brokers.

auth_options.label: JWT Token (in password field)
auth_options.description: Some brokers accept JWT in the password field of CONNECT. Configure token in credential.

auth_options.label: Anonymous
auth_options.description: No authentication — for development/testing brokers only.

name: IMAP Email
setup_hint: Provide IMAP server host and port (993 for TLS). For Apple iCloud: imap.mail.me.com with app-specific password. For Gmail: imap.gmail.com with XOAUTH2 or app password.

auth_options.label: Username + Password
auth_options.description: IMAP LOGIN with username and password over TLS.

auth_options.label: XOAUTH2 (Gmail, Outlook)
auth_options.description: Gmail and Outlook support IMAP XOAUTH2. Provide OAuth token in credential.

name: Firecrawl
description: Firecrawl web scraping and crawling API
setup_hint: SaaS: sign up at firecrawl.dev, get API key (starts with fc-). Self-hosted: `docker compose up` from the Firecrawl repo (port 3002). Pass key as Bearer token.

auth_options.label: API Key (SaaS)
auth_options.description: Sign up at firecrawl.dev, get fc- prefixed API key, use as Bearer token.

auth_options.label: Self-Hosted Token
auth_options.description: Set FIRECRAWL_API_KEY env var in Docker, use same value as Bearer token.

name: Crawl4AI
setup_hint: Self-hosted only: `docker run -d -p 11235:11235 --shm-size=1g unclecode/crawl4ai:latest`. OpenAPI docs at /docs. Optional JWT auth via POST /token.

auth_options.label: JWT Token
auth_options.description: POST /token with credentials to get JWT, use as Bearer. Optional — can run without auth.

auth_options.label: No Auth (local)
auth_options.description: For local/trusted network deployments without authentication.

name: Apify
description: Apify cloud web scraping and automation API
setup_hint: Sign up at apify.com, get API token from Console > Settings > Integrations. Pass as Bearer token. Runs Crawlee-based actors in the cloud.

name: ScrapingBee
setup_hint: Sign up at scrapingbee.com, get API key. Pass as `api_key` query parameter. Single endpoint: GET /api/v1?api_key=KEY&url=TARGET.

name: Browserless
setup_hint: SaaS: get token at browserless.io. Self-hosted: `docker run -p 3000:3000 -e TOKEN=my-token ghcr.io/browserless/chrome`. Pass token as `?token=` query param or Bearer.

auth_options.label: Token (query param)
auth_options.description: Append ?token=YOUR_TOKEN to all requests.

auth_options.label: Bearer Token
auth_options.description: Pass token as Authorization: Bearer header.

name: Jina Reader
description: Jina Reader URL-to-markdown and search API
setup_hint: Simplest: GET https://r.jina.ai/{url} works with no auth (20 RPM). For higher limits, get free key at jina.ai and pass as Bearer token.

auth_options.label: No Auth (20 RPM)
auth_options.description: Works immediately — just prefix any URL with https://r.jina.ai/. Limited to 20 requests/minute.

auth_options.label: API Key (500+ RPM)
auth_options.description: Get free key at jina.ai/?sui=apikey for 500 RPM (Reader) / 100 RPM (Search).

name: Bright Data
description: Bright Data web scraping and proxy API
setup_hint: Sign up at brightdata.com, get API key from Control Panel > Settings > Users. 660+ pre-built dataset scrapers available. Pass as Bearer token.

name: FTP/FTPS
setup_hint: Provide FTP server host, port (21 for FTP, 990 for implicit FTPS, 21 with STARTTLS for explicit FTPS), username and password. For FTPS, the engine uses TLS encryption.

auth_options.label: Username + Password
auth_options.description: FTP LOGIN with username and password.

auth_options.label: Anonymous FTP
auth_options.description: Anonymous access (username: anonymous, password: email or empty).
